overview.description: Hidden Rung (or Hidden Trump) is a popular South Asian trick-taking game, part of the Court Piece (Rang) family. It is played by four players in two fixed partnerships. The game is unique for its 'hidden' trump mechanic: the trump suit is determined by a card selected from the caller's first five cards and placed face-down, remaining unknown until a player is first unable to follow suit.

history.origins: Part of the Sar-Andaz or Court Piece family of games popular in the Indian subcontinent. It share roots with Whist and Bridge but features regional batch-dealing and trump-selection traditions.
timeline: 19th Century: Variations of Rang/Court Piece are established in Northern India.
20th Century: Hidden Rung emerges as a popular social variant, adding tension to the trump reveal.
Modern Era: Remains a staple of social life in Pakistan, Northern India, and Persian-speaking regions.
history.evolution: Developed from the standard 'Sir' or 'Rang' games where the trump is called aloud. The hidden element was likely added to increase the depth of deduction and defensive signaling.
history.cultural: Commonly played at family gatherings and social clubs. It is often played with a high degree of speed and theatricality.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs. East-West).
setup.equipment: 52-card deck and a way to track tricks (or 'Courts').
setup.dealing: The dealer deals 5 cards to each player in the first batch. The player to the dealer's right (Trump Caller) selects their hidden trump. The remaining cards are then dealt in batches of 4 until all cards are distributed (13 per player).

rules.objective: A partnership aims to win the majority (at least 7) of the 13 tricks. Special bonuses (Courts) are awarded for winning 7 consecutive tricks or 7 tricks led by the same team.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Trump Selection**: The caller chooses a card from their first 5 and places it face-down. This suit is the 'Hidden Rung'. 2. **Leading**: The caller leads the first trick. 3. **Following**: Players must follow suit if possible. 4. **Revealing Trump**: If a player cannot follow suit, they may ask the caller to reveal the trump. The caller turns the hidden card face-up. 5. **Winning Tricks**: Before the reveal, the highest card of the suit led wins. After the reveal, the highest trump wins (or highest cards of suit led if no trumps played).
keyRules: Trumps cannot be played to a trick until they have been revealed.
Once revealed, a player void in the led suit MUST play a trump if they have one.
The hidden trump card itself can be used to win a trick once revealed.
If a team wins the first 7 tricks consecutively, it is a 'Court' (instant game win).

strategy.basic: As the caller, choose a suit that is both long (many cards) and strong (high cards). If you don't reveal too early, you might catch an opponent's Ace with a low trump.
strategy.intermediate: If your partner is the caller, try to lead suits where you have strength to draw out defenders' cards before the trump is revealed.
strategy.advanced: Defenders should attempt to force the trump reveal by leading suits they suspect the caller is short in. This removes the 'ambush' potential of the hidden suit.
tips: Don't reveal the trump on a low-value trick if you can help it.
Track which suits have been led; the caller is likely void in a suit they haven't led but refuse to reveal trump on.
Save high non-trump cards for after the trumps have been depleted.

list.name: Double Sir
list.description: Tricks are only picked up when a player wins two consecutive tricks.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Double Sir differs in trick collection rules; engine overrides for heap pickup logic to be added when implementing.

list.name: Satat
list.description: A variant where the hidden trump card is not revealed to everyone, but the caller just announces if the played card trumps it.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Satat uses different trump reveal and 2-of-hearts rule; overrides to be added when variant is implemented.

difficulty.easy: Follows suit; reveals trump immediately when unable to follow; no partnership awareness.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable trump selection; saves trump for high cards; basic partnership lead signaling.
difficulty.hard: Sophisticated deduction of hidden trump based on lead patterns; strategic delay of reveal; counts all cards; simulates potential trump suit outcomes.

considerations: AI must handle the 'Partially Observable' state of the trump suit.
Inference engine for caller's likely suit selection.
Defense must evaluate the risk of 'revealing' vs. 'playing low' on a led high card.

customActions.description: Turn the hidden trump card face up when a player is void in the suit led.
customActions.constraints: Only allowed when a player cannot follow suit for the first time.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card deck is used, with no jokers. The deck has four French suits of thirteen cards each; all fifty-two cards are dealt and used in play. There are no wild cards.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs. Each suit has thirteen cards; suit is used for following and for building sequences in the hidden rung layout.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks from Ace (high) down to two (low) in each suit. There are thirteen ranks per suit; ranking determines the order of cards in sequences and in play.

hero.title: HIDDEN RUNG
hero.subtitle: South Asian Court Piece
hero.tagline: Deduce the hidden trump, outplay your rivals, and rule the court.

synthesis.shortDescription: A tense partnership trick-taking game from the Indian subcontinent where the dealer's partner chooses a hidden trump that stays face-down until the first void. Strategic, social, and deeply rewarding.

prompts.human: Welcome to Hidden Rung. Choose your hidden trump card carefully. Partner, watch the leads—can you figure out our secret suit before the reveal?
prompts.ai: Game: Hidden Rung (Court Piece). 4 players, 2 teams. Caller picks face-down trump from first 5 cards. Play follows Whist rules until a player is void; caller then reveals the trump. Objective: Win 7+ tricks.

scoring.description: Based on number of tricks won (of 13). Winning 7 consecutive tricks or 7-0 is a 'Court'.
scoring.winCondition: The first partnership to win the required number of tricks or score a 'Court'.
